clue.text: Force inferior grass in plant container

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for force in physics
something inferior is lower in rank or quality
pot and grass are both slang names for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone forces a poor-quality grass into a pot meant for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the thing being planted, but here it is slang for cannabis, also called pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot for flowers is the everyday container that holds a plant's soil and roots.

clue.text: One of Aesop's perhaps beginning to feel fit

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of feel is used

parts.note: fit and able both mean capable or in condition to do something

explanation.surface: Someone starts to feel fit, much like a character in an old moral tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek storyteller whose short moral tales with animal characters carry his name; 'perhaps' marks this as an example.

clue.text: Job is a non-starter before retainer becomes alert

indicators.note: before puts the shortened word ahead of the next piece in the down answer
a non-starter here is a word that has lost its start, so the first letter of Job goes

parts.note: a retainer is an old word for a servant kept in a household

explanation.surface: An applicant fails to get a job, and a hired hand becomes more watchful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a non-starter' removes the J of JOB, leaving OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone observant notices things, which is what being alert or watchful means.

clue.text: Just flat end had broken

parts.note: a flat surface is an even one

indicators.note: broken means the letters of end had are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: The flat end of something has been broken, and that is only fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns END HAD into HANDED. 'Just' looks like 'merely' at the start of the surface, but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A just decision is fair and impartial, treating all sides equally.

clue.text: Something played with cards -could be bridge

definitions.meaning: a card game in which players try to reach a total of twenty-one, also called blackjack
a flat-bottomed boat used to support a temporary floating bridge

explanation.surface: Bridge is a game played with cards, so this looks like a card-game riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge suggests the card game, which fits the first half, but the second sense is a boat used to build a floating bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game of reaching twenty-one, and a floating support for a military bridge, share this name.

clue.text: Shoe found in coach

definitions.meaning: a sports shoe or running shoe
someone who trains athletes or teams

explanation.surface: A shoe is left behind on a coach journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests the bus, but it is the sports instructor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports shoe has this name, and so does a sports coach who drills athletes.

clue.text: Kelvin rejected American girl's grilled dish

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

indicators.note: rejected is taken as thrown back, so the word for the girl is read backwards

parts.note: babe is American slang for a girl or sweetheart; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A man named Kelvin is turned down by an American girl who cooked him a grilled meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns BABE round to EBAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of meat grilled on a skewer make this dish.

clue.text: Lisper's smacker for friends and acquaintances

indicators.note: someone with a lisp says th where an s sound should be, changing how the word is pronounced

parts.note: a smacker is slang for a loud kiss

explanation.surface: A lisping person blows a kiss to friends and family.
explanation.walkthrough: A lisper says KISS as 'kith', so the SS becomes TH.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'kith and kin' means friends and relations; the first word refers to friends, neighbours and acquaintances.

clue.text: Sharp chance after first of boundaries

indicators.note: after places the chance word beneath the single letter in this down answer
the first of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of boundaries counts

parts.note: a chance and a risk are both a gamble or possibility of loss

explanation.surface: A batter takes a sharp chance after hitting boundaries at cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk wind or manner is sharp, quick and lively.

clue.text: Get a ball arranged before English game

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the English abbreviation
arranged means the letters of get a ball are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone collects a ball and sets up an English game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns GET A BALL into BAGATELL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a table game in which balls are struck into numbered holes, a forerunner of pinball.

clue.text: Pour fat over model in station

indicators.note: in tells us the model's letter sits inside the word for station

parts.note: a base is a station, such as a military or research post
the Model T was the famous early Ford car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: Someone pours fat over a model at a station.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T was Henry Ford's early mass-produced car, so 'model' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten roasting meat with its own juices or fat is the cookery verb meant.

clue.text: A close shave but rang in the new

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of rang in the are made into something fresh, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A narrow escape is had while the bells rang in the New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns RANG IN THE into NEAR THING; 'but' is a link. The surface suggests ringing in the New Year.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape, where disaster was only just avoided, is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Heartbroken, Bob is on the way to this planet

definitions.text: on the way to this planet

indicators.note: broken means the letters of heart are reassembled in another order

parts.note: the first part of the clue word Heartbroken supplies these letters
to bob is to bounce or leap, which is also to bound

explanation.surface: A heartbroken man called Bob is heading home to this planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartbroken' splits into HEART and the anagram signal 'broken', which turns HEART into EARTH. 'Bob' looks like a name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft heading towards our planet is described as homeward to Earth with this word.

clue.text: Satirical comment on Sunday outfit

indicators.note: on places the abbreviation next to the outfit word

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothes, an outfit, especially sports clothing

explanation.surface: Someone passes a satirical remark about another's Sunday best.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch mocking someone or something is a satirical piece.

clue.text: Try cascade out with some one easily frightened

indicators.note: out signals the letters of try cascade being thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone timid is urged to try a waterfall with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TRY CASCADE; 'with some' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward or timid person is called this in playground slang.

clue.text: Irish river has wrong two numbers on

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of has are put in the wrong order

parts.note: N is a standard abbreviation for number, so two numbers give two Ns

explanation.surface: An Irish river carries two wrong numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns HAS into SHA.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river in Ireland flows through Limerick to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Kept up, having played about

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for played goes around up

parts.note: to sport is to play or frolic, so played gives sported
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone kept going, having played around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept up' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Kept' alone; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep someone, providing for them financially, is to maintain or provide for them.

clue.text: Returned later to cover Channel Islands story

indicators.note: to cover means the reversed word wraps around the islands' abbreviation
returned means sent back, so the following word is read backwards

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey

explanation.surface: Someone came back later to report on a Channel Islands story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns LATER into RETAL, which goes around CI. The Channel Islands are British Crown dependencies off the coast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed account or narration of events, as in a recital of grievances, is a story.

clue.text: Fungus gadget used by Wind in the Willows character?

indicators.note: a tool used by someone is that person's tool, so the possessive comes first

parts.note: Toad is the boastful hero of The Wind in the Willows; the possessive is supplied by used by
a gadget is a tool or device

explanation.surface: A gadget used by Mr Toad of the children's book turns out to be a fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wind in the Willows is Kenneth Grahame's classic children's book; a gadget used by Toad is Toad's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an umbrella-shaped mushroom, usually poisonous.

clue.text: Long-suffering medical case is clear to receive iodine

indicators.note: to receive means the word for clear takes in the element's symbol

parts.note: patent means obvious or clear
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A long-suffering hospital case is clearly in need of iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tolerant and uncomplaining is long-suffering, and a person under a doctor's care is a medical case.

clue.text: Visitor to the old city is on time

indicators.note: on places the time letter beneath the rest in this down answer

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, the crossword's usual old city

explanation.surface: A visitor to an ancient city arrives on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling for pleasure is a sightseer or holidaymaker.

clue.text: Spoil the opening in Kent resort

parts.note: to spoil something is to mar it
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: Someone spoils the opening of a resort in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; Margate is a seaside town there. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town on the north coast of Kent is a holiday destination.

clue.text: Cards handed out wrongly here — pass up unfinished wood

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is lopped off the word for pass up

parts.note: to pass up a chance is to miss it
deal is fir or pine wood

explanation.surface: Someone passes on a half-built wooden table where cards were dealt badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the last S off MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: An error in distributing playing cards to players is this mistake.

clue.text: Exclusive stories don't have small caps? Sorry-my mistake

indicators.note: don't have means the following letters are missing from the word for exclusive stories

parts.note: scoops are exclusive news stories
SC is the printers' abbreviation for small capitals

explanation.surface: A newspaper apologises that its exclusive stories were printed without small capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is the printing abbreviation for small capitals, letters in capital form but of lower-case height.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is said when one makes a slip or blunder, an apology for an error.

clue.text: Fat derives from fruit pie initially

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of pie

explanation.surface: Weight gain comes from eating fruit pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derives from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump means rounded or chubby, carrying extra weight.

clue.text: Bid, I sussed out, is supported financially

indicators.note: out signals the letters of bid i sussed are shaken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bidder works out who is being propped up with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BID I SUSSED; 'is' is a link. 'Sussed out' looks like the slang for 'worked out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A business given grants by the state is propped up by public money.

clue.text: Moves quickly in pub game

definitions.meaning: the game of throwing small pointed missiles at a board, played in British pubs

explanation.surface: Someone moves fast around a pub game.
explanation.definitionFit: It means dashes swiftly, and is also the throwing game played at a board in British pubs.

clue.text: Scrap short holiday

indicators.note: short means the holiday name is cut down, losing its end

parts.note: Whitsun is the British spring holiday around Pentecost

explanation.surface: A short holiday is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitsun, seven weeks after Easter, was traditionally a British bank holiday; cutting it short leaves WHIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny bit, as in 'not a jot', is a scrap or iota.

clue.text: Put one's finger on wire which marks edge of playing area

definitions.text: which marks edge of playing area

parts.note: to put one's finger on something is to touch it
a line is a wire, as in a telephone line

explanation.surface: Someone touches a wire that marks the boundary of a sports pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and rugby, the boundary along each side of the pitch is marked by this.

clue.text: Singers to some extent find echo irritating

indicators.note: to some extent says only a part of the following words is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Some singers find an echo irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of people singing together, especially in church, is this body.

clue.text: Remove drug from store?

parts.note: de- is the prefix meaning remove, as in defrost
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to take drugs out of a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link; read the answer as DE-POT, to take the pot away.
explanation.definitionFit: A warehouse or storehouse for goods is this.

clue.text: Swiss archer least disposed to pass on malicious stories

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple from his son's head

indicators.note: disposed here means arranged, so the letters of least are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: The Swiss archer is least inclined to spread nasty gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' turns LEAST into TALES; 'least disposed' reads as 'least willing'. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To gossip or inform on others is to spread rumours and reveal secrets.
